components.note: 讠 (speech) — 诺 relates to a spoken promise or agreement.
若 (ruò) gives a rhyme close to nuò, sharing a related initial.
A pictograph of a cross-shaped building, possibly an altar or temple floor plan; the character was later adopted to write 'Asia' (亚洲) and the unrelated meaning 'second, next.'

example.hanzi: 诺亚方舟的故事家喻户晓。
example.pinyin: Nuòyà fāngzhōu de gùshì jiāyùhùxiǎo.
example.english: The story of Noah's Ark is well known to every household.
example.fact: The Epic of Gilgamesh, a Mesopotamian poem recorded on clay tablets around 2100 BC, contains a flood narrative strikingly similar to the biblical story of Noah — a man named Utnapishtim builds a boat to save his family and animals from a divine flood. Many scholars believe the biblical account and the Gilgamesh flood story share a common origin in even older Sumerian flood traditions from the Tigris-Euphrates river valley, a region prone to catastrophic flooding.

components.note: 灬 (fire) — 煎 relates to cooking with heat.
前 (qián) gives a sound distantly related to 煎's reading jiān, having drifted apart over time.
饣 (food) — 饼 names a type of food, a flat cake.
并 (bìng) gives a sound close to bǐng, sharing the same rhyme with a different tone.

example.hanzi: 妈妈早上给我做了煎饼当早饭。
example.pinyin: Māma zǎoshang gěi wǒ zuò le jiānbǐng dāng zǎofàn.
example.english: Mom made jianbing for me as breakfast this morning.
example.fact: The golden-brown crust that forms when a batter like jianbing hits a hot pan is caused by the Maillard reaction, a chemical reaction between amino acids and sugars first described by French chemist Louis-Camille Maillard in 1912. It's the same reaction responsible for the flavor of seared steak, toasted bread, and roasted coffee beans, and it only kicks in above roughly 140°C (280°F).

components.note: 气 (simplified from 氣) depicts rising wisps or vapor, like breath or steam drifting upward — a simple picture of air or gas.
王 (a variant of 玉, meaning jade) — 球 originally referred to a round piece of jade, extended to mean 'ball, sphere'
求 (qiú) gives the sound — 球 is also pronounced qiú, an exact match

example.hanzi: 生日派对上挂满了五颜六色的气球。
example.pinyin: Shēngrì pàiduì shàng guà mǎn le wǔyánliùsè de qìqiú.
example.english: The birthday party was decorated with balloons of all colors.
example.fact: In June 1783, French brothers Joseph-Michel and Jacques-Étienne Montgolfier launched the first public demonstration of an unmanned hot air balloon in Annonay, France. Just months later, in November 1783, they sent the first humans aloft in a balloon flight over Paris, launching the era of human flight decades before the airplane.

components.note: 日 (sun) — 星 relates to bright heavenly bodies like the sun and stars
生 (shēng) gives a sound close to 星's reading xīng
月 (moon) — 期 relates to time measured by the moon's cycles, like a period or term.
其 (qí) gives a hint of the sound — 期 is pronounced qī, a connection that has shifted slightly in tone.
二 is simply two horizontal strokes stacked together — the most direct way to picture the number two, following the same pattern as 一 (one) and 三 (three).

example.hanzi: 我们每个星期二都有游泳课。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen měi gè xīngqī'èr dōu yǒu yóuyǒng kè.
example.english: We have swimming class every Tuesday.
example.fact: In English, Tuesday is named after Tiw (or Tyr), the Norse god of war and justice, echoing the Roman naming of the day after Mars, the god of war (reflected in the French mardi and Spanish martes). The seven-day week itself traces back to ancient Babylon, which associated each of the seven visible 'planets' — including the sun and moon — with its own day.

components.note: 阝 (a mound, used in place names) anchors 那 as originally the name of a location. Over time the character was borrowed away from that place name to serve as the demonstrative pronoun 'that,' the meaning it carries in modern words like 那位 and 那儿.

The left-hand element is close in sound to nà and supplied the original pronunciation for the place name. That phonetic role is the only reason it survives in the modern character, since its literal meaning was lost long ago.
亻 (person) — 位 relates to a person's location.
立 (to stand) — the spot where a person stands gave 位 its meaning 'position' or 'place,' and later, a polite measure word for people.

example.hanzi: 那位老师教得非常认真。
example.pinyin: Nà wèi lǎoshī jiāo de fēicháng rènzhēn.
example.english: That teacher teaches very conscientiously.
example.fact: The University of Bologna, founded in 1088 in Italy, is generally considered the oldest continuously operating university in the world. It began as a student-run guild that hired its own teachers, a structure almost the reverse of a modern university, where the institution hires the faculty.

components.note: 人 (person), doubled — one person shown following another depicts the idea of accompanying or coming from somewhere.
大 (big) — in 头's simplified form, this element is linked to the idea of 'high' or topmost, since the head sits at the top of the body.

example.hanzi: 电脑死机了，我只好从头再做一次。
example.pinyin: Diànnǎo sǐjī le, wǒ zhǐhǎo cóngtóu zài zuò yí cì.
example.english: The computer crashed, so I had to start over from the beginning.
example.fact: Many older computer systems store time as a 32-bit signed integer counting seconds since January 1, 1970 — a scheme that will overflow at 03:14:07 UTC on January 19, 2038, an event engineers call the 'Year 2038 problem.' It's a direct descendant of the Y2K bug, and some embedded systems with long service lives, like industrial controllers, are still being patched today to survive it.

components.note: 严 is a simplified form of the traditional 嚴, which pictured many mouths (吅) calling out commands over a cliff (厂), evoking a stern voice issuing orders from on high. The simplification kept only a schematic trace of that image, leaving 严 to carry the meaning 'strict, severe.'

厂 (a cliff or overhang) sits atop the character. In the traditional form 厲, the element beneath it depicted a scorpion under a rock ledge — something dangerous and to be feared, which is the root of 厉's meaning 'severe, fierce.'

example.hanzi: 他对孩子的教育方式非常严厉。
example.pinyin: Tā duì háizi de jiàoyù fāngshì fēicháng yánlì.
example.english: His approach to educating his children is very strict.
example.fact: In the 1960s, developmental psychologist Diana Baumrind identified four parenting styles based on studies of preschoolers — authoritarian, authoritative, permissive, and neglectful — finding that children raised by strict but responsive 'authoritative' parents tended to fare better than those raised by harshly controlling 'authoritarian' ones. Her framework remains one of the most cited models in developmental psychology today.

components.note: 玉 (jade, shown without its dot) represents something valuable.
厶 beneath suggests something slipping away privately, giving 丢 its meaning 'to lose, to throw away.'
丿 (something falling) — an object slipping away.
夫 (a hand/person) — the object slipping out of a hand, giving 失 its meaning 'to lose.'

example.hanzi: 他的护照在旅途中不小心丢失了。
example.pinyin: Tā de hùzhào zài lǚtú zhōng bù xiǎoxīn diūshī le.
example.english: His passport was accidentally lost during the trip.
example.fact: Each year, airlines mishandle tens of millions of checked bags worldwide, though the rate has fallen sharply since the 2000s thanks to bar-coded tracking tags introduced across the industry. SITA's annual baggage report has tracked this decline, showing mishandling rates dropping from roughly 18 bags per 1,000 passengers in 2007 to under 6 by the late 2010s.

components.note: 面 was originally a pictograph of a human face, with an outline around an eye — later broadening to mean 'face, surface, side.'
A simple drawing of a swaddled baby — arms reaching out, legs bundled together in a wrap.

example.hanzi: 在中国文化中，面子是一个很重要的概念。
example.pinyin: Zài Zhōngguó wénhuà zhōng, miànzi shì yí gè hěn zhòngyào de gàiniàn.
example.english: In Chinese culture, 'face' is a very important concept.
example.fact: Sociologist Erving Goffman's 1955 essay 'On Face-Work' formalized the idea that all social interaction involves managing one's public image, or 'face' — a concept independently central to many cultures worldwide. Goffman argued that preserving face is a kind of unspoken ritual order that keeps everyday social encounters running smoothly.

components.note: 工 depicts a carpenter's square or workman's tool — a simple shape that came to represent work and labor.

业 is a simplified form of 業, which originally pictured a large notched wooden board used as a base for hanging bells or chimes, or as a work surface for craftsmen. Because the board was tied to a craftsman's trade, the character came to mean 'occupation, business, industry.'

example.hanzi: 这个城市因重工业而繁荣起来。
example.pinyin: Zhè gè chéngshì yīn zhònggōngyè ér fánróng qǐlái.
example.english: This city prospered because of heavy industry.
example.fact: The Industrial Revolution began in Britain in the late 18th century, powered initially by James Watt's improved steam engine, patented in 1769, which dramatically increased the efficiency of converting coal into mechanical work. Within a century, industrialization had transformed textile production, iron manufacturing, and transportation, reshaping the global economy and driving mass urban migration.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 激 originally described water dashing or surging forcefully
敫 (jiǎo) gives a sound distantly related to 激's reading jī, having drifted apart over time
力 (strength) — 励 relates to exerting effort or spurring on strength in others, 'to encourage.'
厉 (lì) gives the sound — an exact match with 励.

example.hanzi: 老师的鼓励激励了他继续努力学习。
example.pinyin: Lǎoshī de gǔlì jīlì le tā jìxù nǔlì xuéxí.
example.english: The teacher's encouragement motivated him to keep studying hard.
example.fact: In 1714, the British Parliament established the Longitude Prize, offering up to £20,000 — a fortune at the time — to anyone who could devise a reliable way to determine a ship's longitude at sea. The prize spurred clockmaker John Harrison to spend decades perfecting the marine chronometer, a breakthrough that transformed ocean navigation.

components.note: 彳 (step/walk) — relates directly to 往's meaning 'to go toward, in the direction of.'
王 (wáng) gives a sound hint — 往 is pronounced wǎng, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.

后 is a merger of two originally separate characters: an ancient pictograph of a ruler issuing commands from a raised mouth, which meant 'queen, empress,' and the unrelated character 後 meaning 'behind, after.' Simplification folded 後 into 后, so the modern character now carries both meanings depending on context.

example.hanzi: 往后我们要更加小心地处理这些数据。
example.pinyin: Wǎnghòu wǒmen yào gèngjiā xiǎoxīn de chǔlǐ zhèxiē shùjù.
example.english: From now on, we need to handle this data more carefully.
example.fact: The European Union's General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), which took effect in May 2018, was one of the first laws to impose steep fines — up to 4% of a company's global annual revenue — for mishandling personal data. It has since influenced similar privacy laws in dozens of countries outside Europe, including Brazil, California, and India.

components.note: 水 depicts a flowing stream, with a central current and ripples or drops branching off to the sides.
手 is a simple picture of an open hand with the fingers spread out.

example.hanzi: 那位水手在海上工作了三十年。
example.pinyin: Nà wèi shuǐshǒu zài hǎishàng gōngzuò le sānshí nián.
example.english: That sailor has worked at sea for thirty years.
example.fact: In 1747, Scottish naval surgeon James Lind conducted one of the first controlled clinical trials, giving groups of scurvy-stricken sailors different remedies and finding that citrus fruit cured the disease fastest. It took the Royal Navy another 40 years to adopt his findings, but once it did, scurvy — which had killed more sailors than combat throughout the Age of Sail — largely disappeared from long voyages.

components.note: 亻 (person) — 使 involves a person carrying out a task.
吏 (a government official) — 使 originally referred to an official sent to carry out orders, giving rise to the meaning 'to make someone do something' or 'to use.'
力 (strength) — 劲 names physical strength or energy.

example.hanzi: 他使劲把门推开了。
example.pinyin: Tā shǐjìn bǎ mén tuī kāi le.
example.english: He pushed the door open with all his strength.
example.fact: The strongest muscle in the human body relative to its size is the masseter, the jaw muscle used for biting, which can exert a force of over 90 kilograms (200 pounds) at the molars in a forceful bite. Overall body strength, however, comes from the coordinated action of hundreds of muscles working together, not any single one.

components.note: 广 (a building or shelter) sets 廉 in the context of a dwelling — the character originally described the sharp corner or edge of a house. That sense of a clean, sharp edge extended figuratively to 'incorruptible, upright,' and separately to 'low-priced.'
兼 (jiān) is close in sound to lián and served as the phonetic component, sharing the same rhyme with a shifted initial consonant.
介 (jiè) gives a sound hint — 价 is pronounced jià, sharing the same initial consonant though the vowel has shifted.

example.hanzi: 这家超市专门出售廉价商品。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā chāoshì zhuānmén chūshòu liánjià shāngpǐn.
example.english: This supermarket specializes in selling low-cost goods.
example.fact: The standardized steel shipping container, introduced by American trucking entrepreneur Malcom McLean in 1956, cut the cost of loading cargo onto ships by roughly 90% compared to the older method of hand-loading loose freight. That single innovation is widely credited with making today's globally sourced, low-cost consumer goods economically possible.

components.note: 耳 is a simplified picture of the outer shape of a human ear.
王 (a variant of 玉, jade) — 环 originally referred to a round jade ring or bracelet
不 (bù) gives a sound distantly related to 环's reading huán, having drifted apart considerably over time

example.hanzi: 她今天戴了一对漂亮的耳环。
example.pinyin: Tā jīntiān dài le yí duì piàoliang de ěrhuán.
example.english: She wore a pair of beautiful earrings today.
example.fact: Ötzi the Iceman, a naturally mummified body found frozen in the Ötztal Alps in 1991 and dated to roughly 3300 BC, had earlobes stretched by earrings measuring 7 to 11 millimeters across — evidence that ear piercing is at least five millennia old. Archaeologists have found gold earrings from Mesopotamia dating back almost as far, showing the practice arose independently across several ancient cultures.

components.note: 人 (people) over 云 (clouds/say) — a picture of people gathering and speaking together, related to 会's meanings 'to meet' and 'to know how to.'
A short stroke placed above a longer one — a simple graphic way to show 'up' or 'above,' contrasted with 下 (down), which flips the strokes.

example.hanzi: 会上，经理宣布了新的销售计划。
example.pinyin: Huì shang, jīnglǐ xuānbù le xīn de xiāoshòu jìhuà.
example.english: At the meeting, the manager announced the new sales plan.
example.fact: Robert's Rules of Order, first published in 1876 by U.S. Army officer Henry Martyn Robert, standardized how meetings and votes should be conducted and remains the most widely used parliamentary procedure manual in the English-speaking world. It was inspired by his frustration after presiding over a chaotic church meeting with no clear rules for debate.

components.note: 亻 (person) ties 体 to the human body, the character's core meaning.

本 (root, foundation) was chosen as a simple, easy-to-write substitute for the complex traditional component 骨 (bone) found inside 體. The swap kept the character recognizable while making it far quicker to write by hand.
贝 (money) — 贴 originally referred to pawning something for money, extending to 'to stick on, to subsidize.'
占 (zhàn) is only distantly related in sound to tiē — the connection has drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 他是一个非常体贴的丈夫。
example.pinyin: Tā shì yí gè fēicháng tǐtiē de zhàngfu.
example.english: He is a very considerate husband.
example.fact: Psychologist Daniel Goleman's 1995 book 'Emotional Intelligence' popularized the idea that skills like empathy and self-awareness matter as much as IQ for personal and professional success. The underlying academic concept had been introduced a few years earlier, in 1990, by psychologists Peter Salovey and John Mayer, who first defined and measured it scientifically.

components.note: 牛 (ox) — 特 originally referred to a male ox singled out for sacrifice, a special animal set apart from the herd.
寺 (sì) gives a hint of the sound — 特 is pronounced tè, a connection that has drifted over time.
宀 (roof) — represents a home or fixed dwelling.
疋 (a foot/person) — a person settling down under a roof gave 定 its meaning 'to decide, to fix, to settle.'

example.hanzi: 这个软件只支持特定的操作系统。
example.pinyin: Zhè gè ruǎnjiàn zhǐ zhīchí tèdìng de cāozuò xìtǒng.
example.english: This software only supports specific operating systems.
example.fact: Unix, the ancestor of Linux, macOS, and Android's core, was created in 1969 by Ken Thompson and Dennis Ritchie at Bell Labs, originally to run on a spare PDP-7 minicomputer after a bigger multi-user project called Multics was abandoned. Its design principles — small, modular programs that each do one thing well — still shape how operating systems are built more than fifty years later.

components.note: 耳 (ear) — an old sense linked shame to the reddening of the ears.
止 (zhǐ) gives a sound close to chǐ, sharing the same rhyme though the initial has shifted.

辰 originally depicted a large clam-shell hoe used for early agricultural work, with 寸 (a hand) below it showing someone gripping the tool. Being forced to labor with such a crude implement, often as punishment, gave 辱 its meaning 'disgrace, humiliation.'

example.hanzi: 战败对这支球队来说是巨大的耻辱。
example.pinyin: Zhànbài duì zhè zhī qiúduì lái shuō shì jùdà de chǐrǔ.
example.english: The defeat was a huge disgrace for this team.
example.fact: Article 231 of the 1919 Treaty of Versailles, often called the 'war guilt clause,' forced Germany to accept blame for World War I and pay reparations, a stipulation many Germans experienced as a profound national disgrace. Historians still debate how much that resentment contributed to the political instability that followed in the 1920s and 1930s.

components.note: 月 (yuè) here actually derives from 肉 (meat) — 有 originally depicted a hand holding meat, meaning 'to possess'; it also lends a loose phonetic connection to yǒu.
龶 depicts a poisonous plant, tying 毒 to its meaning 'poison.'
母 (mǔ) gives a rhyme close to dú, with the initial shifted.

example.hanzi: 小心，这种蘑菇是有毒的。
example.pinyin: Xiǎoxīn, zhè zhǒng mógu shì yǒudú de.
example.english: Be careful, this kind of mushroom is poisonous.
example.fact: The death cap mushroom (Amanita phalloides) is responsible for the majority of fatal mushroom poisonings worldwide, and it closely resembles several edible species, making misidentification easy. Its toxin, amatoxin, attacks the liver but produces no symptoms for 6 to 24 hours after ingestion, a delay that often leads victims to underestimate the danger until serious organ damage has already begun.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 港 names a harbor, a body of water.
巷 (xiàng) reflects the character's historical phonetic root, though the modern reading gǎng has diverged.
口 is a simple picture of an open mouth.

example.hanzi: 上海是世界上最繁忙的港口之一。
example.pinyin: Shànghǎi shì shìjiè shàng zuì fánmáng de gǎngkǒu zhī yī.
example.english: Shanghai is one of the busiest ports in the world.
example.fact: The Port of Shanghai has been the world's busiest container port by cargo volume every year since 2010, handling over 47 million shipping containers in 2022 alone. Much of its capacity comes from the Yangshan Deep-Water Port, an artificial island connected to the mainland by a 32-kilometer bridge, built because the natural harbor near Shanghai was too shallow for the largest modern cargo ships.

components.note: 日 depicts the sun as a circle with a dot or short stroke inside — a simplified picture of the sun's disc, later squared off in the standard script.
巾 (cloth) — 常 originally referred to a long skirt or banner made of cloth, later coming to mean something 'usual' or 'ordinary.'
尚 (shàng) gives a hint of the sound — 常 is pronounced cháng, a connection that has drifted over time.

example.hanzi: 跑步已经成了他日常生活的一部分。
example.pinyin: Pǎobù yǐjīng chéng le tā rìcháng shēnghuó de yí bùfen.
example.english: Running has become part of his daily life.
example.fact: In 2017, the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine was awarded to Jeffrey Hall, Michael Rosbash, and Michael Young for discovering the molecular mechanisms that control the circadian rhythm — the roughly 24-hour internal clock that governs daily patterns of sleep, hormone release, and body temperature in nearly all living organisms. Their research began with fruit flies and identified a specific gene, period, whose protein levels rise and fall in a daily cycle.

components.note: The bowl-shaped body of an old stemmed serving dish.
A lid or rim on top of the dish.
A simple drawing of a swaddled baby — arms reaching out, legs bundled together in a wrap.

example.hanzi: 奶奶在花园里种了很多豆子。
example.pinyin: Nǎinai zài huāyuán lǐ zhòng le hěn duō dòuzi.
example.english: Grandma planted a lot of beans in the garden.
example.fact: Bean plants, like other legumes, host colonies of Rhizobium bacteria in nodules on their roots that convert atmospheric nitrogen into a form plants can use, a process called nitrogen fixation. Farmers have exploited this for millennia by rotating legume crops with cereals, naturally replenishing soil fertility without synthetic fertilizer.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 撒 describes scattering something by hand.
散 (to scatter, to disperse) — combined with the hand 扌, it gave 撒 its meaning 'to scatter, to release.'
A person's crouching body shape.
Water — represents the liquid being passed.

example.hanzi: 小狗到处撒尿来标记自己的地盘。
example.pinyin: Xiǎogǒu dàochù sāniào lái biāojì zìjǐ de dìpán.
example.english: The puppy urinates everywhere to mark its territory.
example.fact: Many mammals, including dogs and wolves, use urine to mark territory because it carries pheromones and other chemical signals that convey information about an individual's identity, sex, and reproductive status to other animals. Wolves in a pack will often mark boundaries with urine at regular intervals along well-traveled trails, effectively posting chemical 'signs' that discourage rival packs from intruding.

components.note: 土 (here representing a person swinging their arms, not its usual meaning 'earth') — depicts someone in motion.
止 (a foot) — combined with the moving figure above, 走 shows a person walking or running.
A simple line drawing of a person's legs seen from the side, used to depict a human being.

example.hanzi: 老板生气地让他马上走人。
example.pinyin: Lǎobǎn shēngqì de ràng tā mǎshàng zǒurén.
example.english: The boss angrily told him to leave immediately.
example.fact: The phrase 'quiet quitting' went viral in 2022 to describe employees who do only the minimum required by their job description, though the underlying behavior — psychologists call it 'work disengagement' — has been studied by organizational researchers since at least the 1990s. Gallup's long-running workplace surveys have consistently found that only around a third of employees globally report feeling genuinely engaged at work.

components.note: 弓 (bow) — the weapon being drawn.
丨 depicts the taut drawstring being pulled back — giving 引 its meaning 'to pull, draw out, attract.'

用 is thought to be a pictograph of a wooden bucket or a fenced enclosure used for containing livestock, an everyday tool put to practical use. That everyday utility is the likely root of 用's meaning 'to use, to apply.'

example.hanzi: 这篇论文引用了很多权威资料。
example.pinyin: Zhè piān lùnwén yǐnyòng le hěn duō quánwēi zīliào.
example.english: This paper cites a lot of authoritative sources.
example.fact: In 2005, physicist Jorge Hirsch introduced the h-index, a single number meant to capture both the productivity and citation impact of a researcher's published work. Despite well-documented flaws — it ignores field-specific citation norms and rewards long careers over recent quality — the h-index remains one of the most widely used metrics in academic hiring and promotion decisions.

components.note: 忄 (heart) shows 怜 relates to an emotion.
令 (lìng) gives a sound close to lián, differing mainly in the vowel and tone.
忄 (heart) — 悯 describes an inner feeling, compassion.
闵 (mǐn) gives the sound — an exact match with 悯's reading.

example.hanzi: 她对流浪的动物充满了怜悯之心。
example.pinyin: Tā duì liúlàng de dòngwù chōngmǎn le liánmǐn zhī xīn.
example.english: She is full of pity for stray animals.
example.fact: In the early 1990s, neuroscientists in Parma, Italy, led by Giacomo Rizzolatti, discovered 'mirror neurons' in macaque monkeys — brain cells that fire both when an animal performs an action and when it merely observes another individual performing that same action. The finding sparked decades of research into whether a similar mechanism in humans underlies empathy and our capacity to feel compassion for others' suffering.

components.note: 才 depicts a young sprout just breaking through the soil — new growth came to represent budding talent or ability.
Originally a drawing of a bear, with 厶 as its head, ⺼ as its body, and 匕匕 as its claws; the picture was later borrowed to mean 'ability, to be able to.'

example.hanzi: 每个孩子都有自己独特的才能。
example.pinyin: Měi gè háizi dōu yǒu zìjǐ dútè de cáinéng.
example.english: Every child has their own unique talents.
example.fact: The idea that mastering a skill requires roughly 10,000 hours of practice was popularized by journalist Malcolm Gladwell in his 2008 book 'Outliers,' drawing on research by psychologist Anders Ericsson into expert violinists. Ericsson himself later pushed back on the oversimplified rule, emphasizing that the quality of practice — specifically, deliberate practice with focused feedback — matters far more than raw hours logged.

components.note: 亻 (person) — 信 relates to a person's word.
言 (speech, words) — a person standing behind their spoken word gave 信 its core meaning 'trustworthy, to believe,' which later extended to a written message one can trust, a 'letter.'
亻 (person) — 件 relates to a person separating something into parts.
牛 (ox) — dividing an ox into pieces gave 件 its meaning of an individual 'item' or 'piece,' now used as a measure word for objects and matters.

example.hanzi: 邮递员每天早上送来大量的信件。
example.pinyin: Yóudìyuán měitiān zǎoshang sòng lái dàliàng de xìnjiàn.
example.english: The postman delivers a large amount of mail every morning.
example.fact: The Penny Black, issued in Britain in May 1840, was the world's first adhesive postage stamp, and its introduction let senders prepay postage rather than making recipients pay on delivery. The reform, championed by Rowland Hill, was credited with dramatically increasing mail volume across Britain within just a few years.

components.note: 电 (simplified from 電) depicts a bolt of lightning — since lightning is a natural form of electricity, the character came to mean 'electricity.'
纟 (thread) — relates directly to 线's meaning 'line, thread, wire.'
戋 (jiān) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from xiàn.

example.hanzi: 施工队正在检查地下的电线。
example.pinyin: Shīgōngduì zhèngzài jiǎnchá dìxià de diànxiàn.
example.english: The construction crew is inspecting the underground electric wires.
example.fact: In the late 1880s, Thomas Edison and George Westinghouse fought the so-called 'War of Currents' over whether homes should be wired for direct current (DC), which Edison championed, or alternating current (AC), backed by Westinghouse and Nikola Tesla. AC eventually won out because it could be transmitted efficiently over much longer distances at high voltage, and it remains the standard for power grids worldwide today.

components.note: 日 is the semantic element, tying the character's meaning to the sun.
暴's everyday reading is "bào" (as in 曝光, "to expose"), which matches this character's alternate reading exactly; the "pù" reading used here is a more literary variant.
儿 (a person) — shown carrying a torch overhead, the source of 光's meaning 'light, brightness.'
火 (fire) — the torch's flame, the thing giving off the light.

example.hanzi: 这张照片曝光过度，看起来太亮了。
example.pinyin: Zhè zhāng zhàopiàn bàoguāng guòdù, kàn qǐlái tài liàng le.
example.english: This photo is overexposed and looks too bright.
example.fact: The oldest surviving photograph made in a camera, taken by French inventor Nicéphore Niépce around 1826–27, required an exposure time of roughly eight hours, during which the sun visibly moved across the sky and lit both sides of the courtyard in the image. Modern digital cameras can achieve a comparable exposure in a fraction of a millisecond.

components.note: 彳 depicts a step with the left foot; together with 亍 (a step with the right foot), 行 shows a person walking or moving.
亍 depicts a step with the right foot, complementing 彳 to form the idea of walking or travel.
禾 (grain) — 程 originally named a unit for measuring grain, extended to 'process, journey, degree.'
呈 (chéng) gives the sound — 程 is also pronounced chéng, an exact match.

example.hanzi: 这次旅行的行程安排得非常紧凑。
example.pinyin: Zhè cì lǚxíng de xíngchéng ānpái de fēicháng jǐncòu.
example.english: The itinerary for this trip is scheduled very tightly.
example.fact: Marco Polo's journey from Venice to the court of Kublai Khan, recounted in 'The Travels of Marco Polo,' took roughly four years to complete via the Silk Road, covering thousands of kilometers by camel caravan, horse, and boat. His account, written after he returned to Europe in 1295, became one of the most influential travel narratives in shaping European curiosity about Asia.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 撞 describes striking or bumping into something with force.
童 (tóng) is only distantly related in sound to zhuàng — the connection has drifted apart over time.
手 (hand) — in the traditional form 擊, 手 contributed the meaning of striking with force, the source of 击's meaning 'to hit, strike.'

example.hanzi: 两辆车在十字路口发生了撞击。
example.pinyin: Liǎng liàng chē zài shízìlùkǒu fāshēng le zhuàngjī.
example.english: The two cars collided at the intersection.
example.fact: The Chicxulub impact, a roughly 10-kilometer-wide asteroid that struck what is now Mexico's Yucatán Peninsula about 66 million years ago, released energy equivalent to billions of atomic bombs and is widely believed to have triggered the mass extinction that wiped out most dinosaurs. The crater it left behind, over 150 kilometers across, was only confirmed via geological and gravitational surveys in the 1990s.

components.note: 也 is thought to have originally been a pictograph of a coiled snake, or possibly a ladle, though scholars disagree on the exact image. Whatever its original referent, the character was borrowed purely for its sound to serve as the grammatical particle meaning 'also, too,' the meaning it retains today.
女 (woman) — represents a mother.
子 (child/son) — a mother together with her child was seen as an image of goodness, giving 好 its meaning 'good.'

example.hanzi: 你不想去也好，我们可以下次再约。
example.pinyin: Nǐ bùxiǎng qù yěhǎo, wǒmen kěyǐ xiàcì zài yuē.
example.english: It's fine if you don't want to go; we can plan for another time.
example.fact: The 1978 Camp David Accords, brokered by U.S. President Jimmy Carter between Israel and Egypt, took 12 days of intense negotiation at the presidential retreat to produce a framework for peace, ending decades of conflict between the two nations. It remains one of the most significant diplomatic agreements in modern Middle Eastern history.

components.note: 木 (tree) — provides the base image of a tree.
一 (a line) marks the base of the trunk, highlighting the roots — giving 本 its meaning 'root, origin, source.'
忄 (heart/mind) — 性 relates to inner nature or character.
生 (shēng) gives a hint of the sound — 性 is pronounced xìng, a related sound though the initial has shifted.

example.hanzi: 善良是他的本性。
example.pinyin: Shànliáng shì tā de běnxìng.
example.english: Kindness is his true nature.
example.fact: The Minnesota Study of Twins Reared Apart, launched in 1979 by psychologist Thomas Bouchard, tracked identical twins separated at birth and raised in different families, finding striking similarities in personality, IQ, and even specific habits despite years apart. The research became a landmark case for the influence of genetics — an inborn 'nature' — on human behavior, though scientists agree environment still plays a substantial role.

components.note: 雨 (rain) — 露 names a form of moisture related to weather.
路 (lù) gives the sound — an exact match with 露.

营 is a simplified form of 營, which originally showed a ring of torches (represented by a doubled fire radical) surrounding a cluster of dwellings — a lit, guarded encampment at night. That image of a defended camp is the source of 营's meanings 'camp' and, by extension, 'to operate, to manage.'

example.hanzi: 这个周末我们打算去山里露营。
example.pinyin: Zhè gè zhōumò wǒmen dǎsuàn qù shān lǐ lùyíng.
example.english: This weekend we plan to go camping in the mountains.
example.fact: Yellowstone, established in 1872, was the world's first national park, created specifically to protect its geothermal features — including the geyser Old Faithful — from private development. Its creation inspired the modern national park movement, which now protects wilderness areas, many of them popular camping destinations, in more than 100 countries.

components.note: 艹 (grass) — 草 refers to grass or plants
早 (zǎo) gives a sound close to 草's reading cǎo, sharing a similar historical pronunciation
土 (earth) — 坪 names a flat, open piece of ground.
平 (píng) gives the sound — an exact match with 坪.

example.hanzi: 孩子们在草坪上玩得很开心。
example.pinyin: Háizimen zài cǎopíng shàng wán de hěn kāixīn.
example.english: The children had a great time playing on the lawn.
example.fact: The modern lawnmower was invented in 1830 by English engineer Edwin Beard Budding, who adapted a rotary blade mechanism used to trim the nap off woolen cloth in textile mills. Before his invention, maintaining a lawn required scything by hand or grazing livestock, which meant manicured grass lawns were largely a luxury reserved for the wealthy.

components.note: 十 (ten) — suggests something repeated many times.
口 (mouth) — a story passed down through ten generations of mouths gave 古 its meaning 'old, ancient.'
艹 (plant) reflects 董's original meaning related to a type of plant, later used for "to direct, supervise" and as a surname.
重 (zhòng) gives a sound distantly related to dǒng, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 他收藏了很多明清时期的古董。
example.pinyin: Tā shōucáng le hěn duō Míng Qīng shíqī de gǔdǒng.
example.english: He collects many antiques from the Ming and Qing dynasties.
example.fact: Ming dynasty (1368–1644) blue-and-white porcelain was so prized across Asia, the Middle East, and Europe that it inspired imitation industries in Persia and the Netherlands (Delftware), centuries before global trade was common. Genuine pieces routinely sell at auction today for millions of dollars, and experts still rely on details like glaze crackling and cobalt pigment composition to distinguish authentic antiques from later reproductions.

components.note: 夂 (a foot, to walk) — 各 pictures people arriving from different directions.
口 (mouth) — different people speaking gave 各 its meaning 'each' or 'every,' emphasizing individual distinctness.
丨 (a vertical tally mark) over 人 (person) — suggests counting people one by one, fitting 个's role today as Mandarin's most common general measure word.

example.hanzi: 这个问题涉及社会的各个方面。
example.pinyin: Zhè gè wèntí shèjí shèhuì de gègè fāngmiàn.
example.english: This issue involves every aspect of society.
example.fact: In a honeybee colony, individual workers specialize in different roles — nursing larvae, foraging, guarding the hive, or cleaning — and can shift between these jobs as they age or as the colony's needs change, a division of labor biologists call 'polyethism.' Coordinating each of these separate roles without any central planner is what lets a colony of tens of thousands function as a single, resilient unit.

components.note: 面 was originally a pictograph of a human face, with an outline around an eye — later broadening to mean 'face, surface, side.'
木 (tree) ties 条 to a slender branch or twig, the character's original meaning, later extended to any long, thin strip and to a measure word for such items.
The traditional form 條 paired 木 with the phonetic component 攸 (yōu), whose pronunciation has since drifted well away from the modern reading tiáo.

example.hanzi: 妈妈煮了一碗热腾腾的面条。
example.pinyin: Māma zhǔ le yì wǎn rèténgténg de miàntiáo.
example.english: Mom cooked a steaming bowl of noodles.
example.fact: In 2005, archaeologists excavating the Lajia site in northwestern China's Qinghai province discovered a bowl containing the remains of noodles made from foxtail and broomcorn millet, dated to roughly 4,000 years ago. The find pushed back the earliest known evidence of noodle-making by about 2,000 years and settled part of a long debate over whether noodles originated in China or the Middle East.

components.note: 画 depicts a picture set within a frame — the traditional form 畫 additionally showed a hand holding a brush above it.
宀 (roof) — 家 is about a home, the space under a roof.
豕 (shǐ, 'pig') supplies the ancient sound for 家; keeping a pig under one's roof was also a practical sign of a household in ancient China, though the modern readings jiā and shǐ no longer rhyme.

example.hanzi: 这位画家的作品在世界各地展出。
example.pinyin: Zhè wèi huàjiā de zuòpǐn zài shìjiè gèdì zhǎnchū.
example.english: This painter's works are exhibited all over the world.
example.fact: Dutch painter Vincent van Gogh created more than 2,000 artworks in just over a decade but is believed to have sold only a single painting, 'The Red Vineyard,' during his lifetime. Today his works, including 'The Starry Night' and 'Sunflowers,' are among the most valuable and recognizable paintings in the world, with some selling at auction for over $80 million.

components.note: 纟 (silk/thread) — 纯 originally described unmixed, undyed silk thread, extending to 'pure, unmixed.'
屯 (tún) gives a sound distantly related to chún, having drifted apart over time.
氵 (water) — 洁 describes something washed and made clean and pure.
吉 (jí) gives a sound close to jié, sharing the initial — the rhyme has drifted slightly from í to ié.

example.hanzi: 孩子的心灵总是那么纯洁。
example.pinyin: Háizi de xīnlíng zǒngshì nàme chúnjié.
example.english: A child's heart is always so pure.
example.fact: Ultrapure water used in semiconductor manufacturing must have virtually every dissolved mineral, ion, and particle removed — far cleaner than drinking water — because even microscopic contaminants can ruin the nanometer-scale circuits etched onto a silicon wafer. Producing it requires a multi-stage process of reverse osmosis, deionization, and ultrafiltration that can take a facility days to fully purify a single batch.

components.note: 阝 (mound, place) shows 陪 relates to being present alongside someone somewhere.
咅 gives a sound distantly related to péi, having drifted apart over time.
亻 (person) — 伴 describes a person accompanying another.
半 (bàn) is an exact match for the sound of 伴.

example.hanzi: 狗是人类忠实的陪伴动物。
example.pinyin: Gǒu shì rénlèi zhōngshí de péibàn dòngwù.
example.english: Dogs are loyal companion animals for humans.
example.fact: Genetic studies suggest dogs were domesticated from wolves somewhere between 15,000 and 40,000 years ago, making them the oldest domesticated animal species and predating agriculture by thousands of years. Some researchers argue the relationship began when wolves that tolerated human camps and scavenged food scraps gradually evolved into companions, long before any deliberate breeding took place.

components.note: 无 is a simplified form of 無, which originally depicted a dancer holding decorated tassels or sleeves in each hand, performing a ritual dance. The character was later borrowed purely for its sound to write the unrelated word for 'without, nothing,' and that borrowed meaning eventually took over entirely.
阝 (a mound/place) — 限 relates to a boundary or limit on a place
艮 (gèn) gives a loose sound connection to 限's reading xiàn

example.hanzi: 宇宙的边界似乎是无限的。
example.pinyin: Yǔzhòu de biānjiè sìhū shì wúxiàn de.
example.english: The boundary of the universe seems to be unlimited.
example.fact: Cosmologists distinguish between the 'observable universe,' which has a finite radius of about 46 billion light-years because light from farther away hasn't had time to reach us since the Big Bang, and the universe as a whole, whose total extent is unknown and could in fact be infinite. This distinction means that even an infinite universe could appear to have a boundary simply because of the finite speed of light.

components.note: 田 (field) — represents farmland.
力 (strength/effort) — someone strong enough to work the fields gave 男 its meaning 'male, man.'
子 (child) — 孩 relates directly to children
亥 (hài) gives a sound close to 孩's reading hái
A simple drawing of a swaddled baby — arms reaching out, legs bundled together in a wrap.

example.hanzi: 那个男孩子在公园里踢足球。
example.pinyin: Nà gè nánháizi zài gōngyuán lǐ tī zúqiú.
example.english: That boy is playing soccer in the park.
example.fact: Modern association football's first standardized rules were drawn up in 1863 in London when representatives of several English football clubs met to form the Football Association, settling long-running disputes over whether players could carry the ball with their hands. Clubs that insisted on keeping the handling rule split off to form rugby football instead.

components.note: 穴 (a cave or hole) sets the scene of a cramped, confined dwelling.
力 (strength, effort) — someone straining their utmost within a cramped, cave-like space gave 穷 its meaning 'to exhaust, to reach the limit,' and by extension 'poor, destitute.'
A simple line drawing of a person's legs seen from the side, used to depict a human being.

example.hanzi: 这个慈善组织专门帮助穷人。
example.pinyin: Zhè gè císhàn zǔzhī zhuānmén bāngzhù qióngrén.
example.english: This charity organization specifically helps poor people.
example.fact: According to World Bank data, the share of the world's population living in extreme poverty (on less than roughly $2.15 a day) fell from about 38% in 1990 to under 9% by the late 2010s, even as the global population grew by billions. Much of that decline was driven by rapid economic growth in China and other parts of East Asia.

components.note: Mouth — calling out is done with the mouth.
Gives the sound huàn, matching the character's reading.
酉 (wine jar) — 醒 originally described sobering up from drink, extending to 'to wake up.'
星 (xīng) gives a sound close to xǐng, sharing the same syllable body and differing mainly in tone.

example.hanzi: 闹钟的声音把我从梦中唤醒了。
example.pinyin: Nàozhōng de shēngyīn bǎ wǒ cóng mèng zhōng huànxǐng le.
example.english: The sound of the alarm clock woke me from my dream.
example.fact: Rapid eye movement (REM) sleep, the stage most associated with vivid dreaming, was first identified in 1953 by researcher Eugene Aserinsky and his advisor Nathaniel Kleitman, who noticed periodic rapid eye movements in sleeping subjects using an electroencephalograph. Waking someone during REM sleep tends to produce the most detailed dream recall, while waking during deep non-REM sleep often leaves people groggy and disoriented.

components.note: 力 (strength) — 加 pictures adding one's effort to a cause.
口 (mouth, words) — combining strength with words of support gave 加 its meaning 'to add' or 'to increase.'
禾 (grain, a growing rice or wheat plant) — 利 pictures a harvest.
刂 (knife) — cutting grain at harvest time was a clear benefit or gain, giving 利 its meaning 'profit' or 'advantage.'
礻 (spirit/altar) — 福 relates to blessings granted by the spirits
畐 (fú) gives the sound — an exact match with 福's reading fú

尸 (a seated or reclining figure) — 尼 originally depicted two people close together, sitting side by side. The character was later borrowed for its sound alone, used today mainly in transliterations (as in 尼亚) and in 尼姑, 'Buddhist nun.'
A pictograph of a cross-shaped building, possibly an altar or temple floor plan; the character was later adopted to write 'Asia' (亚洲) and the unrelated meaning 'second, next.'

example.hanzi: 加利福尼亚以阳光和海滩闻名。
example.pinyin: Jiālìfúníyà yǐ yángguāng hé hǎitān wénmíng.
example.english: California is famous for its sunshine and beaches.
example.fact: The California Gold Rush began in January 1848 when gold was discovered at Sutter's Mill, drawing roughly 300,000 people to the territory within a few years and transforming it into a state admitted to the Union in 1850. California's coastal redwoods, found nowhere else on Earth in the wild, include the tallest trees known to exist, some exceeding 115 meters (380 feet) in height.

components.note: 土 (earth) — 基 relates to the ground or foundation something is built on.
其 (qí) gives a hint of the sound — 基 is pronounced jī, a connection that has shifted significantly over time.
金 depicts a bell or metal casting mold, with dots representing droplets of molten metal — a picture linked to metal and, later, specifically gold.
人 (people) over 云 (clouds/say) — a picture of people gathering and speaking together, related to 会's meanings 'to meet' and 'to know how to.'

example.hanzi: 这家基金会致力于资助医学研究。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā jījīnhuì zhìlìyú zīzhù yīxué yánjiū.
example.english: This foundation is dedicated to funding medical research.
example.fact: The Nobel Foundation was established in 1900 to manage the fortune left by Swedish inventor Alfred Nobel, whose 1895 will directed that his estate fund annual prizes in physics, chemistry, medicine, literature, and peace. Nobel reportedly created the prizes partly in reaction to a premature obituary that labeled him a 'merchant of death' because of his invention of dynamite.
